column1: Score each line 0-4. Be honest — an inflated score just wastes your own money later.
0 = not at all  |  1 = barely  |  2 = partly  |  3 = mostly  |  4 = fully

column2: Question
column4: What a 4 looks like

column2: Do you know where your key business data actually lives?
column4: You could list every system and who owns it, today

column2: Is that data accessible without a manual export?
column4: An API or direct query exists; nobody emails a spreadsheet

column2: Is it accurate enough to act on without cleaning?
column4: You would make a pricing decision on it unreviewed

column2: Do you have a lawful basis to process it this way?
column4: Documented, and your DPO has seen it

column2: Can you name the 3 processes that cost most staff time?
column4: With hours per week attached, measured not guessed

column2: Are those processes written down?
column4: A new hire could follow the document unaided

column2: Are they consistent between people?
column4: Two staff produce the same output from the same input

column2: Do you measure their current cost or duration?
column4: You have a baseline you could compare against later

column2: Does anyone internally use AI tools competently today?
column4: At least one person others already ask for help

column2: Is there a named owner for AI decisions?
column4: One person, not a committee, with authority to stop things

column2: Would staff tell you if a tool was not working?
column4: They have, recently, and nothing bad happened to them

column2: Is there budget for training rather than only tools?
column4: A real line item, not an intention

column2: Is there a written AI usage policy?
column4: Circulated, acknowledged, and reviewed in the last 6 months

column2: Do staff know what they must not paste into a chatbot?
column4: They could list the categories without prompting

column2: Is there an approved-tools list with business accounts?
column4: Provisioned by IT, training disabled

column2: Is there a route to report a mistake safely?
column4: Someone has used it and was not punished

column2: Can you state the problem before naming a tool?
column4: The problem was written down before any vendor was contacted

column2: Do you know what success would look like numerically?
column4: A specific metric and a target, agreed in advance

column2: Have you agreed what would make you stop?
column4: A kill criterion exists and someone is willing to apply it

column2: Is there a budget holder who has actually approved spend?
column4: Signed off, not verbally encouraged

column2: TOTAL (out of 80)
Not ready. Fix data access and process documentation first. AI on undocumented, inconsistent processes automates the inconsistency.
Partially ready. Pick ONE well-documented process and pilot there. Do not start a programme.
Ready for real pilots. Your constraint is now choosing well and measuring honestly, not capability.
Ready to scale. Your risk has shifted from 'can we' to 'are we doing the right ones' — start killing weak projects faster.

column1: If you score 0-1 on 'Have you agreed what would make you stop?', treat your total as provisional.
Organisations without a kill criterion do not fail at AI — they succeed slowly and expensively at the wrong thing.
